item.title: Scientists removed 285,000 fish from Wisconsin lake; yellow perch rose 788%
item.description: Scientists removed about 285,000 centrarchid fish from Wisconsin’s McDermott Lake between 2018 and 2021 to see if reducing competition and predation could help walleye recover. The experiment sharply reduced several fish species and saw yellow perch numbers rise by about 788%. However, researchers found no detectable natural walleye recruitment, showing that removing centrarchids alone did not restore the lake’s walleye population.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Miami Beach reefs built in 1998 later attracted 97,826 fish from 146 species
item.description: A 2002 study examined 12 artificial reefs built off Miami Beach using limestone boulders, concrete-gravel aggregate and concrete mixed with waste tyre chips. Divers surveyed the reefs every two months from October 1998 to February 2001, recording fish species, numbers and sizes, along with spiny lobsters. They counted 97,826 fish from 146 species. The researchers found no significant difference in fish abundance, biomass or species richness between the three reef materials. However, comparisons before and after deployment showed that the artificial reefs increased local fish abundance and species richness.

item.title: SpaceX sends $4.3bn Roman Space Telescope to look for 'weird, rare’ stars, planets
item.description: SpaceX has achieved another milestone by successfully launching NASA's Roman Space Telescope into orbit. This groundbreaking observatory is designed to delve into the mysteries of distant planets and the enigmatic forces of dark energy. Its expansive field of view is one hundred times that of the Hubble Space Telescope, enabling it to work in tandem with other instruments, paving the way for extraordinary cosmic discoveries awaiting our exploration.

item.title: LeBron James’ $25.5m foundation faced criticism: Why did Akron’s school spark questions?
item.description: LeBron James' foundation is dedicated to empowering youth in Akron by providing crucial education and life skills programs. Recently, the I PROMISE School faced challenges due to unsatisfactory state test outcomes. Yet, amidst the critique, the foundation remains steadfast in its support for students and their families. A new collaboration with Nike introduces swimming lessons, focusing on building confidence and enriching life experiences beyond academics.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5m charity under scrutiny: Why did less go to charity?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation is facing scrutiny over its reported spending between 2021 and 2024. The nonprofit raised $1.5 million and spent about $1.1 million, with $469,000 listed for management and $446,000 for charity. Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes disputed the figures, saying some charitable operational costs were misclassified. He said management fees dropped to zero in 2025 as the foundation works to improve transparency and governance.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $2.75M community impact: How is he giving back to Kansas City?
item.description: The Patrick Mahomes Foundation has made a significant impact in Kansas City by distributing nearly $2.75 million in grants. A notable achievement includes a $1 million investment in the Martin Luther King Jr. Park. Additionally, the foundation has provided countless meals and free eye exams for families. Their '15 for 15' program creates valuable opportunities for underserved youth, ensuring Mahomes leaves a meaningful legacy in the community.

This initiative aims to improve road safety and worker well-being.

item.title: 'November is a priority’: Trump aides push to contain Iran war until midterm elections
item.description: Top Trump aides push to prevent Iran war escalation before November elections. The administration is focusing on economic pressure to secure concessions from Iran. Recent exchanges of strikes have increased tensions between the US and Iran. Military readiness and depleted munitions stockpiles also constrain White House strategy. America's Gulf allies are urging the White House to de-escalate the conflict.

item.title: 'New peaks of lethality': IAF tests Khagantak-243; all about long range glide bomb
item.description: The Indian Air Force has achieved a major milestone by successfully testing the Khagantak-243 glide bomb. This homegrown weapon enhances India's stand-off precision strike capability, covering distances of over 140 km once released from an aircraft. Developed in partnership by Bharat Electronics Limited and JSR Dynamics, this test underscores India's commitment to defence innovation.

China seeks to expand its influence and safeguard vital shipping routes. Egypt is diversifying its international partnerships by strengthening ties with Beijing.

item.description: Noida police arrested three individuals for an inter-district theft gang. The accused allegedly targeted locked flats and stole valuables from housing societies. Police recovered cash, jewellery, and electronic devices from the arrested suspects. The gang members reportedly wore masks and caps to avoid CCTV detection. Investigators are now working to identify other gang members and trace stolen goods.

item.title: World war 2: The deadliest conflict in human history ended 81 years ago today
item.description: Eighty-one years ago, on September 2, 1945, the curtains fell on World War II, the most devastating conflict in history. Triggered by Nazi Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939, this global war escalated when Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, drawing the United States into the fray. The tide turned with the Allied forces’ victories, leading to Germany's surrender in May 1945.

This trend indicates a divergence between the luxury and middle-market housing segments.
